sources.text: Main text decoder only. Large matrices are modeled at BF16 with FP32 accumulation. Reference FP32 compressor, hyper-connection, router and output projections use the generic FP32 compute ceiling. The release checkpoint uses FP8 and routed FP4; its physical weights, quantization kernels and auxiliary scales require their own configuration.

BF16 window, compressed latent and indexer caches use active batch lanes, a provisioned local ring and completed global rows. Compressor value and score buffers are FP32. The causal equations support a logical query chunk after past tokens; the release reference uses an initial prefill followed by one-token calls.

Sparse attention uses a materialized rectangular score and probability reference, with exact useful causal pair counts. Weight traffic assumes each active routed expert is read once and uses an upper bound on distinct experts. Nonlinear, selection, fake quantization and Sinkhorn use explicit operation proxies. MTP, kernel scheduling, data-dependent sparsity, YaRN table generation are outside this preset.

Local equations bind allocated request, head and expert extents. Lookup and sparse expert reads use explicit traffic equations. Link rates and analytical work proxies describe the configured estimate.

Each rank holds whole attention heads and matching output groups. Indexer query heads contribute FP32 partial scores, reduced before candidate selection or masking. Window, compressed latent, index K and compressor state are replicated, with one backing per shared cache on each rank. The row-parallel output partial uses an FP32 AllReduce before resuming the BF16 residual path.

Each EP rank owns a contiguous, equal count of routed experts. Each token keeps its global Top-K, with per-rank route budgets balanced by quotient and remainder. Allocated slots use ceil(K/EP). Useful work and sparse gathers use valid slots. The shared expert is replicated and added after reducing FP32 routed partials.

Routed-expert TP shards matched gate and up channels, SwiGLU results and down-projection input channels. TP peers within each owner group duplicate its route metadata. FP32 routed partials are summed across owner and feature ranks before the replicated shared expert is added.

Non-quantized matrices retain the sampled checkpoint storage dtype. Routed memory traffic uses the touched fraction of local weights and scales. Published quantized matrices are available via the fixed weight preset.
